O. Recently, I travelled from the Old Delhi railway station to Dehradun in a two-tier, air-conditioned train compartment.

Q. It was a deeply unsettling experience.

questions.solution: O starts the paragraph and introduces the primary setting using a clear sentence that sets the scene: “Recently, I travelled from the Old Delhi railway station to Dehradun in a two-tier, air-conditioned train compartment.”

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. His business was so successful that Mark was able to _________ at the age of 50.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

His business was so successful that Mark was able to _________ at the age of 50.
questions.solution: Retire' will be used because it means to end one’s working life and live a relaxed life. The sentence states that Mark's business was so successful that he was able to stop working at the age of 50, making 'retire' the correct choice here. 'Admit' means to accept or confess, which is irrelevant to the context. 'Give up' means to quit or surrender, which doesn’t align with the idea of business success. 'Succeed' means to achieve success, but it doesn’t complete the meaning of the sentence correctly.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please bring some milk from ______ refrigerator in the kitchen.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please bring some milk from ______ refrigerator in the kitchen.
questions.solution: The' will be used because it specifies "refrigerator" as the one located in the kitchen. 'The' is used when we talk about something specific. 'An' is used before singular nouns starting with a vowel sound. However, 'refrigerator' does not begin with a vowel sound. 'No article required' is incorrect because an article is necessary before 'refrigerator'. 'A' is used for nonspecific singular nouns. Here, the refrigerator is specific, making 'A' inappropriate.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. P. The smell would soon be followed by a whirring sound of the beans getting ground. My mother would rotate the handle of a mechanical grinder fixed on a kitchen shelf. Q. After a while, the comforting aroma of freshly brewed filter kaapi would waft in the air. R. ‘Coffee is just a drink, but kaapi is an emotion’, proclaimed an advertisement. S. Having switched to mostly masala chai and occasionally instant coffee, I remembered the post siesta afternoons in my home town and hallucinated on the aroma of roasted coffee beans.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

P. The smell would soon be followed by a whirring sound of the beans getting ground. My mother would rotate the handle of a mechanical grinder fixed on a kitchen shelf.

Q. After a while, the comforting aroma of freshly brewed filter kaapi would waft in the air.

R. ‘Coffee is just a drink, but kaapi is an emotion’, proclaimed an advertisement.

S. Having switched to mostly masala chai and occasionally instant coffee, I remembered the post siesta afternoons in my home town and hallucinated on the aroma of roasted coffee beans.
questions.solution: S follows R, providing a personal recollection related to the quote. The narrator remembers the aroma of roasted coffee beans and the post-siesta afternoons, setting a vivid scene that connects to the emotional impact of "kaapi" mentioned earlier.
